name: Dip
pattern: Vertical push down: you hold your body up on straight arms, then bend the elbows and let the shoulders go into extension, and push back up.
setup: Grip the bars about shoulder width, jump or step up to straight arms.
Shoulders down away from your ears, chest proud.
Knees bent or legs straight, ankles together; brace your trunk.

steps.text: Start on straight arms, body still, shoulders pushed down.
Bend your elbows and lean slightly forward, elbows pointing back, not out.
Stop when your upper arms are about level with the bars or a bit below, shoulders still down.
Push the bars down until your arms are straight again.

cues.cue: Lower until upper arms are about parallel to the bars, not deeper.
cues.why: The dip takes the shoulder to about 65-70° of extension; deeper loads the front of the shoulder and the pec tendon.

cues.cue: Keep shoulders down, away from your ears.
cues.why: The serratus anterior and lower trapezius work hard to control the shoulder blade, more so when tired.

cues.cue: Elbows point back, close to your sides.
cues.why: Typical bar-dip abduction is only about 30°; wide elbows move the load onto the shoulder.

cues.cue: Lean forward about 20-40° for chest, stay upright for triceps.
cues.why: Bar dips show about 37° of forward lean at the bottom; the lean shifts work to the chest.

cues.cue: Lower in 2 seconds, no drop and bounce.
cues.why: Pec major ruptures are reported during dips; the fast stretch at the bottom is the risky part.

breathing: Breathe in on the way down, out as you push up.

tempo.note: Slow down, press up in about 1 s.

mistakes.name: Going too deep
mistakes.looks: Shoulders sink far below the elbows and roll forward.
mistakes.fix: Stop with upper arms about level with the bars.
mistakes.why: End-range shoulder extension loads the front capsule and the pec tendon.

mistakes.name: Shoulders shrug up
mistakes.looks: Shoulders rise toward the ears, neck looks short.
mistakes.fix: Push the bars down, shoulders away from ears.
mistakes.why: The shoulder blade loses its depressed, stable position.

mistakes.name: Elbows flare out
mistakes.looks: Elbows point to the sides as you go down.
mistakes.why: More abduction and rotation at the bottom shifts the work from the triceps to the shoulder.

safety: Shoulder pain at the bottom: shorten the range or use a dip machine or band.
Bench dips put the shoulder in more extension than bar dips; skip them if the front of the shoulder hurts.
Add weight only once you can do 10-12 clean bar dips.

variants.change: Lean forward about 30-45°, elbows can open a little: more chest.
Trunk near upright, elbows tight: more triceps.
Rings move: peak triceps activity like bar dips, but more stabiliser muscles work; turn the rings out at the top.
Weight on a belt or between the feet; same form.
Knee pad, counterweight or band helps you up: same arm path.
Seated dip machine: same arm path, trunk supported.

subtypes.name: Bench dip
subtypes.change: Hands behind you on a bench or chair, hips just in front, legs out. Lower by bending the elbows.

subtypes.name: Scapula dip
subtypes.change: Arms stay straight; only the shoulders move: sink up toward your ears, then push down tall.

subtypes.name: Dip hold
subtypes.change: Hold the top or the bottom position still, shoulders down.

subtypes.name: Korean dip
subtypes.change: Hands on a bar behind your back: very large shoulder extension; advanced only.

motion.basis: Bottom position measured in mckenzie2022b (bar dip): shoulder extension 68 ± 11°, abduction 31 ± 4°, elbow flexion 115 ± 9°, thoracic lean 37 ± 10°, external rotation 9 ± 14°. Bench dip needs more shoulder extension (mckenzie2022a); its angles are estimates. Scapula was not measured in any study: values are estimates (depressed at the top, slight downward rotation and anterior drift as the shoulder extends).

sources.cite: McKenzie A, Crowley-McHattan Z, Meir R, Whitting J, Volschenk W. Bench, bar, and ring dips: do kinematics and muscle activity differ? Int J Environ Res Public Health. 2022;19(20):13211.
